gaps.sentence: The witness ___ the police that he knew nothing.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody that... — the personal object 'the police' requires told, not said.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: "Do not touch the wire!" — She warned me ___ the wire.
gaps.explanation: 'Warn somebody not to do' — 'not' comes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
She ___ that she would be waiting by the main entrance.
gaps.hint: say takes no personal object here
gaps.explanation: Say (that)... without a personal object; 'told that' is impossible without the object.
